extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / PR practitioners who pitch journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Best-practice guidance for building media lists and emailing pitches tailored to different outlet types, plus relationship-building and a short quality checklist for PR practitioners pitching journalists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with 20-30 reporters who actively cover your space
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with 20-30 reporters who actively cover your space
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a focused, manageable list of reporters rather than blasting many contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Cision/Muck Rack for contact info, not bulk lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Cision/Muck Rack for contact info, not bulk lists
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage reputable media databases to find accurate contact details but avoid importing large untailored lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read 5+ recent articles per reporter before adding
rubrics_metrics.description: Read 5+ recent articles per reporter before adding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify a reporter's beat and recent coverage to ensure relevance and to craft a personalized pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize by: beat, frequency, openness to PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize by: beat, frequency, openness to PR
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize your media list so you can match story types and timing to each reporter's preferences and schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Update quarterly — beats shift constantly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regularly refresh the media list to reflect reporter role changes and shifting beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: news + specific angle (under 60 chars)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject line: news + specific angle (under 60 chars)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convey the news and the angle succinctly; keep subject lines short to increase open rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Greeting: First name only
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the reporter's first name for a personable but professional opening; avoid generic salutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 1: Why I'm pitching THIS reporter (refer to recent work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 1: Why I'm pitching THIS reporter (refer to recent work)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show you've read their recent work and explain why this pitch fits their beat to demonstrate relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 2: The news (one specific paragraph)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the news clearly and concisely in one focused paragraph — avoid long-winded context in the opener.

rubrics_metrics.name: Para 3: What I can offer (interview, demo, exclusive, data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Para 3: What I can offer (interview, demo, exclusive, data)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out available assets or exclusives so the reporter knows how you can facilitate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sign-off: Direct phone, email, calendar link
rubrics_metrics.description: Sign-off: Direct phone, email, calendar link
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for the reporter to respond or book time by including direct contact methods and scheduling links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether you've actually read their work
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you've actually read their work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters judge pitches on evidences of familiarity with their past coverage—personalization matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether your story fits their beat
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether your story fits their beat
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the pitch aligns with the reporter's coverage area to avoid obvious mismatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether you understand their deadline cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you understand their deadline cycle
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing and lead times matter; demonstrate awareness of when reporters work and file stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether you can deliver on what you offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you can deliver on what you offer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only promise interviews, visuals, exclusives, or data if you can reliably provide them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether you're a relationship or transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether you're a relationship or transaction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters prefer sources who build long-term relationships over one-off transactional outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be a useful source on stories you're NOT in
rubrics_metrics.description: Be a useful source on stories you're NOT in
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add value by offering expertise and leads beyond your immediate pitches to build credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send relevant items even when not pitching your client
rubrics_metrics.description: Send relevant items even when not pitching your client
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic non-pitch outreach keeps relationships warm and positions you as a helpful resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect 'no' gracefully
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle rejection professionally to maintain rapport for future opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remember personal details (when appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate personalization (e.g., referencing past conversations) can strengthen relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connect them with sources outside your client roster
rubrics_metrics.description: Connect them with sources outside your client roster
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making useful introductions increases your value as a connector and resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch by 10am for next-day consideration (daily newspapers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For daily newspapers, send pitches early in the day to be considered for the next day's coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local angle essential (daily newspapers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newspapers prioritize local relevance—frame the story with a clear local hook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick turnaround on requests (daily newspapers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect rapid follow-up and be ready to provide materials on tight deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple sources expected (daily newspapers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daily reporters typically require corroborating sources; be prepared to supply more than one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry expertise expected (trade publications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trades expect subject-matter depth—use knowledgeable spokespeople and technical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical depth welcome (trade publications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide technical detail and data when pitching trade outlets; they value expertise over generalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longer lead times (1-2 weeks) (trade publications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for longer editorial cycles for trades; allow time for review and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product reviews possible (trade publications)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trades may accept product review pitches — offer review units and technical specs when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual story essential (broadcast TV)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TV needs strong visuals or demonstrable on-camera elements to justify coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talent available for live shot (broadcast TV)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure spokespeople can appear live and are prepared for broadcast interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing tied to news cycle (broadcast TV)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TV bookings are highly time-sensitive; coordinate quickly around breaking or scheduled segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: B-roll and sound bites useful (broadcast TV)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ready-to-use visual and audio assets to increase the chance of TV pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch the host, not network (podcasts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address your pitch to specific hosts and tailor the angle to that host's show and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to recent episodes first (podcasts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize yourself with format, guests, and tone before pitching to propose a good fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific episode angle (podcasts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose a concrete segment idea that fits the show's format to make it easy for hosts to say yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spokesperson must be conversational (podcasts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Podcasts favor guests who speak easily and engage in unscripted conversation rather than reads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tee up to 3 talking points (podcasts)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a small set of clear, compelling talking points to help the host and prepare the guest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-built, current media list (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A high-quality pitch program uses curated, up-to-date lists rather than generic lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized opening referencing recent work (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective pitches open with a personalized reference to the reporter's recent articles to show relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story angle, not generic announcement (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pitches should present a clear, newsworthy angle rather than generic press-release language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right format for outlet type (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content, lead time, and assets to the expectations of the target outlet (e.g., TV vs. trade).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship-first approach (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize ongoing relationships with reporters over one-off transactional contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-through on what you offer (Quality Rubric)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliver promised interviews, assets, or exclusives promptly to maintain credibility.
